text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 3 nodes reporting repeated ECC/Xid sequences; elevated container restarts on inference-pool-usw2. Auto-escalation to on-call.

sre-maria: seeing a pattern — ECC correctable errors spike then NV driver resets (Xid 13/31). GPU metrics show kvcache growth and OOM churn.

oncall-alex: paging — I'm on it. tagging @infra-jonah and @prod-eng-tilly

infra-jonah: attaching recent logs: ```
[2026-03-15T02:12:34Z] nv-host: GPU0 ECC SBE corrected count +427
[2026-03-15T02:12:37Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (31): 0000000c GPF on chid 0x1234
[2026-03-15T02:12:37Z] containerd: container runtime: process exited, code=137, reason=OOMKilled
```

prod-eng-tilly: stack traces show long-running KV cache for models with long prefix lengths. suspect runaway prefix caching and batch size.

sre-maria: quick mitigation: cordon nodes gpu-ustack-12..14, drain with graceful 30s to failover requests. I'll open an ops-bridge and start node isolation.

oncall-alex: doing cordon now: `kubectl cordon gpu-ustack-12`

infra-jonah: `kubectl drain gpu-ustack-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` in progress. moving pods -> risk of temporary 502s.

cs-lena: any customer impact so far? Support sees a spike in 504s starting 02:12 UTC on a handful of keys. Not widespread yet but some enterprise customers reported errors.

sre-maria: quick analysis: 0.8% error bump cluster-wide, but 6% on affected AZ. throttling/backpressure triggered in routing which led to container restarts on overloaded backends.

oncall-alex: observed driver reset on gpu-ustack-13 during drain — container restarted twice in 3m.

infra-jonah: running `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` on the node to see if it stabilizes NV driver. also pulling hwmon temps — but temps are normal. suspect transient ECC event.

prod-eng-tilly: suggest deploying a hotfix to serving runtime to reduce per-request KV cache retention for 1 hour window: set KV_CACHE_MAX_PREFIX=128 and BATCH_LIMIT=12 for canary rollout to reduce memory pressure.

sre-maria: agree — canary to 10% traffic and monitor. I'll add an automated fallback rule to route to smaller-quantized model variant if latency spikes.

oncall-alex: I've opened ops-bridge call and added notes. `ops-bridge: https://call.ops/bridge/4171234567`

incident-bot: NOTE: auto-annotations added — tag:gpu-instability, severity:high, mitigation:node-cordon, kvcache-tweak

infra-jonah: after restart, driver logs show repeated Xid 31 but no full GPU panic. nv-host log snippet: ```
Mar 15 02:15:02 gpu-ustack-13 nvidia: Xid (31) 0x00000000: PID 4581: NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 15 02:15:02 gpu-ustack-13 dockerd: container restart (runtime: runc)
```

prod-eng-tilly: rolled canary config to 10% with reduced cache. telemetry: token-level cost down 18% on canary, KV mem usage down 45% so far.

sre-maria: continuing to monitor. planning to drain gpu-ustack-13 too if Xid count doesn't tail off in 10m.

oncall-alex: starting customer comms draft — short note re transient GPU driver errors impacting a minority of inference requests in US-WEST-2; mitigation underway. @cs-lena will you review?

cs-lena: pulling list of impacted customers and request IDs. prepping targeted notifications for customers with >5% error rate.

infra-jonah: FYI I executed a graceful reboot of the node kernel module stack: `sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm` — no kernel oops observed post-reload.

prod-eng-tilly: can we reduce batch window on affected hosts until we get full RCA? Also recommend enabling CPU fallback for long-latency prefixes to avoid repeated GPU retries.

sre-maria: put temporary autoscale increase for dedicated pool to absorb load while we stabilize.

oncall-alex: summary so far for bridge: nodes 12..14 cordoned; canary KV cache reduction at 10%; driver restarted on node-13; customer impact limited but some enterprise keys saw 5-12% error spike.

incident-bot: ACTION REQUIRED: if Xid count does not reduce by 02:35 UTC, escalate to platform-engineering for hardware replacement queue.

infra-jonah: checking BMC for node-13 — ECC counts persist but server sensors normal. filing hardware ticket pre-emptively: `HW-TICKET-98231`

prod-eng-tilly: starting an eval job to reproduce high prefix retention locally with synthetic load so we can test the KV cache boundary patches. will report back in 30m.

sre-maria: handing off to next on-call in 40m. adding runbook notes: drain if Xid>100 in 15m window, cordon and reprovision.

oncall-alex: thanks team — oncall to oncall handoff scheduled at 02:52 UTC. I'll paste notes to incident channel and update the customer comms after cs-lena signs off. :thumbsup:

cs-lena: comms approved. sending targeted emails to 3 customers now.

prod-eng-tilly: reproduced flaky Xid in local env with long prefixes + quantized kernels. filing repo issue and PR with patch: reduce KV retention and add early eviction. PR: `https://git.redwood/serving/PR/7842`

sre-maria: closing bridge in 45m pending stabilization. marking incident as "mitigated — ongoing RCA".

oncall-alex: last check: error rate trending down to baseline on affected keys. I'll leave monitoring alerts in verbose mode for 6h.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. tags:investigation-open, hardware-ticket:HW-TICKET-98231

prod-eng-tilly: follow-ups: hardware soak on node-13, KV cache hard limit rollout staged, add telemetry for ECC burst correlation with batch sizes.

sre-maria: thanks all, great coordination. handing to night shift.

oncall-alex: handoff complete.
